title: Build district walk plans in the background
body:
Offices want help splitting their district into canvassing turfs, and the door knocking create flow currently makes them draw every turf by hand. This adds a district walk plan: the district's rooftop households split into walk areas of about `doorsPerArea` doors (30 to 200, default 60, about a two-hour shift), in walking order. The webapp change to show it comes in a follow-up.

Why it's a background job: building a plan means grouping every household in the district, which is a district-wide warehouse scan that takes several seconds on a large county, and the grouping work grows with the district. None of that should happen inside a request, so the work runs in the queue, the result lives in Postgres, and both routes only touch the `walk_plan` row:

- `POST /v1/contacts/walk-plan` resets the org's one `walk_plan` row to `queued`, clears its old areas, enqueues `WALK_PLAN_BUILD` with only the plan id (grouped per org, deduplicated per request) and returns 202 straight away. It returns 409 while a build is in progress, unless that request is over 30 minutes old (a lost build). If the enqueue fails, the plan is marked `failed`.
- `GET /v1/contacts/walk-plan` reads the stored plan and its areas. 404 before the first request.
- The job (`WalkPlanService.handleQueuedBuild`) reads the cells from Databricks with `buildWalkPlanCellsSql`. The warehouse does the heavy lifting: households grouped into ~200m cells, already sorted into walking order (bands swept back and forth), capped at 10,000 cells with one extra row to detect a clipped district. Node then makes one linear pass (`planWalkAreas`) that yields to the event loop every 1,000 cells, because the queue consumer shares its process with the API's HTTP traffic. The areas are replaced in the same transaction that marks the plan `ready`, and only while the plan still answers the request that queued the job.
- Redelivery is safe. A delivery that dies before the store leaves the plan `building` for the next one, a delivery after the store finds it `ready` and acks, and a failed read or store asks for redelivery until the third delivery (the queue's maxReceiveCount), which marks it `failed`.

New tables `walk_plan` and `walk_plan_area` (migration included, no secret columns). Response and request shapes are in contracts (`WalkPlan.schema.ts`).

Tests: the pass (`walkPlan.util.test.ts`), the SQL builder, the consumer routing, and route tests through the harness covering the gates, the 202 + enqueue, the 409, a full build then read, retry vs last attempt, a failed store on the last attempt, redelivery, re-request, replacing a stale build and enqueue failure. Documented in `src/contacts/docs/http-surface.md`.

+import { z } from 'zod'
+import { BboxSchema } from '../shared/Bbox.schema'
+
+// Households per walk area. Sixty is about a two-hour shift for one
+// canvasser.
+export const WALK_PLAN_MIN_DOORS = 30
+export const WALK_PLAN_MAX_DOORS = 200
+export const WALK_PLAN_DEFAULT_DOORS = 60
+
+export const WalkPlanStatusSchema = z.enum([
+  'queued',
+  'building',
+  'ready',
+  'failed',
+])
+
+export const RequestWalkPlanInputSchema = z
+  .object({
+    doorsPerArea: z
+      .number()
+      .int()
+      .min(WALK_PLAN_MIN_DOORS)
+      .max(WALK_PLAN_MAX_DOORS)
+      .default(WALK_PLAN_DEFAULT_DOORS),
+  })
+  .strict()
+export type RequestWalkPlanInput = z.infer<typeof RequestWalkPlanInputSchema>
+
+// `bbox` spans the centers of the area's ~200m cells.
+export const WalkPlanAreaSchema = z.object({
+  centerLat: z.number().min(-90).max(90),
+  centerLng: z.number().min(-180).max(180),
+  households: z.number().int().positive(),
+  bbox: BboxSchema,
+})
+
+// The district's latest walk plan request. `areas` and `builtAt` stay empty
+// until its build is ready. `truncated` when the district had more cells
+// than one build reads; the areas then cover only the part of the sweep that
+// was read.
+export const WalkPlanResponseSchema = z.object({
+  status: WalkPlanStatusSchema,
+  doorsPerArea: z.number().int(),
+  requestedAt: z.string(),
+  builtAt: z.string().nullable(),
+  truncated: z.boolean(),
+  areas: z.array(WalkPlanAreaSchema),
+})
+export type WalkPlanResponse = z.infer<typeof WalkPlanResponseSchema>

+enum WalkPlanStatus {
+  queued
+  building
+  ready
+  failed
+}
+
+/// An organization's district split into walk areas of about doorsPerArea
+/// rooftop households, built by the WALK_PLAN_BUILD queue job
+/// (src/contacts/services/walkPlan.service.ts). One per organization; a new
+/// request resets it and clears its areas.

+  id               Int            @id @default(autoincrement())
+  createdAt        DateTime       @default(now()) @map("created_at")

+  areas            WalkPlanArea[]
+
+  @@map("walk_plan")
+}
+
+/// One area of a walk plan, in walking order. The bbox spans the centers of
+/// the area's ~200m cells.

+  id         Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
+  walkPlanId Int      @map("walk_plan_id")

+  ordinal    Int
+  households Int
+  centerLat  Float    @map("center_lat")
+  centerLng  Float    @map("center_lng")
+  minLat     Float    @map("min_lat")
+  maxLat     Float    @map("max_lat")
+  minLng     Float    @map("min_lng")
+  maxLng     Float    @map("max_lng")
+
+  @@unique([walkPlanId, ordinal])
+  @@map("walk_plan_area")
+}

 | `POST /v1/contacts/polygon-preview`                                                    | Live count for a boundary drawn over an in-progress list: same unsaved-draft payload and gates as `count`, narrowed by a bbox prefilter plus an in-process ray-cast (people_db has no geometry column, so there is no ST_Contains to run). A boundary can have several parts (`GeoJsonShape` — one `Polygon`, or a `MultiPolygon`), and each part is scanned against its OWN bbox and unioned by person id, so the count is unique across parts and one box around scattered parts never drags most of the district through the cap. Returns `{ count, audienceEmpty }` — `audienceEmpty` separates "your filters match nobody" from "this shape holds none of your audience", which are the same zero on the wire and different problems. +| `POST /v1/contacts/walk-plan`                                                          | Requests the org's walk plan: the district's rooftop households split into walk areas of about `doorsPerArea` (30 to 200, default 60). Resets the one `walk_plan` row to `queued`, clears its areas, enqueues `WALK_PLAN_BUILD` (plan id only, grouped per org) and answers 202 with the plan. Never reads the warehouse itself. 409 while a build is in progress, unless that request is over 30 minutes old (a lost build). An enqueue that fails marks the plan `failed`. A failed read or store asks for redelivery until the third delivery, which marks it `failed`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
 | `GET /v1/campaigns/mine/recommended-lists/:variant/download` (recommendedLists module) | The saved-list CSV for a recommendation not saved yet: resolves the variant's global universe, then `ContactsService.downloadFilter` — `downloadContacts` fed an inline filter, always individual voters (`docs/features/recommended-lists.md`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

Backs the voter data page's recommended-list detail sheet (`docs/features/recommended-lists.md`). Aggregates only, so open to a free campaign like `count`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,240 @@
+import {
+  ConflictException,
+  Injectable,
+  NotFoundException,
+} from '@nestjs/common'
+import { getTime, subMinutes } from 'date-fns'
+import type { WalkPlanResponse } from '@goodparty_org/contracts'
+import {
+  Organization,
+  Prisma,
+  WalkPlan,
+  WalkPlanArea,
+  WalkPlanStatus,
+} from '@/generated/prisma'
+import { createPrismaBase, MODELS } from '@/prisma/util/prisma.util'
+import { QueueProducerService } from '@/queue/producer/queueProducer.service'
+import { MessageGroup, QueueType } from '@/queue/queue.types'
+import { WALK_PLAN_MAX_CELLS } from '@/peopleDb/databricks/databricksVoterSql.util'
+import { VoterDoorKnockingService } from '@/peopleDb/services/voterDoorKnocking.service'
+import { ContactsService } from './contacts.service'
+import { planWalkAreas } from '../utils/walkPlan.util'
+
+// The queue's maxReceiveCount. The delivery that reaches it marks the plan
+// failed and acks, rather than leaving it building behind a DLQ message.
+export const WALK_PLAN_BUILD_MAX_RECEIVES = 3
+
+const IN_PROGRESS = [WalkPlanStatus.queued, WalkPlanStatus.building]
+
+// A build still in progress this long after its request was lost (every
+// delivery died before the last could mark it failed), so a new request may
+// replace it rather than wait on it forever.
+const STALE_BUILD_MINUTES = 30
+
+const AREAS_PER_INSERT = 2_000
+
+// Up to WALK_PLAN_MAX_CELLS areas, written in AREAS_PER_INSERT batches.
+const STORE_TRANSACTION_OPTIONS = { maxWait: 10_000, timeout: 30_000 }
+
+const toResponse = (
+  plan: WalkPlan,
+  areas: WalkPlanArea[],
+): WalkPlanResponse => ({
+  status: plan.status,
+  doorsPerArea: plan.doorsPerArea,
+  requestedAt: plan.requestedAt.toISOString(),
+  builtAt: plan.builtAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
+  truncated: plan.truncated,
+  areas: areas.map((area) => ({
+    centerLat: area.centerLat,
+    centerLng: area.centerLng,
+    households: area.households,
+    bbox: {
+      minLat: area.minLat,
+      maxLat: area.maxLat,
+      minLng: area.minLng,
+      maxLng: area.maxLng,
+    },
+  })),
+})
+
+// The district split into walk areas, built off the request path: the
+// warehouse groups and orders the district's households, the WALK_PLAN_BUILD
+// job makes one pass over the result and stores the areas, and both routes
+// only read and write the walk_plan row.
+@Injectable()
+export class WalkPlanService extends createPrismaBase(MODELS.WalkPlan) {
+  constructor(
+    private readonly contacts: ContactsService,
+    private readonly voterDoorKnocking: VoterDoorKnockingService,
+    private readonly queueProducer: QueueProducerService,
+  ) {
+    super()
+  }
+
+  async getPlan(organization: Organization): Promise<WalkPlanResponse> {
+    await this.contacts.assertProAccess(organization)
+    const plan = await this.model.findUnique({
+      where: { organizationSlug: organization.slug },
+      include: { areas: { orderBy: { ordinal: Prisma.SortOrder.asc } } },
+    })
+    if (!plan) {
+      throw new NotFoundException('No walk plan has been requested')
+    }
+    return toResponse(plan, plan.areas)
+  }
+
+  async requestPlan(
+    organization: Organization,
+    doorsPerArea: number,
+  ): Promise<WalkPlanResponse> {
+    await this.contacts.assertProAccess(organization)
+    // A district that cannot be read fails here, with the same
+    // VOTER_DATA_UNAVAILABLE as every other people read, rather than in a
+    // job nobody is watching.
+    await this.contacts.resolveEligibleDistrict(organization)
+
+    const organizationSlug = organization.slug
+    const requestedAt = new Date()
+    const request = {
+      status: WalkPlanStatus.queued,
+      doorsPerArea,
+      requestedAt,
+      builtAt: null,
+      truncated: false,
+    }
+    const reset = await this.client.$transaction(async (tx) => {
+      const { count } = await tx.walkPlan.updateMany({
+        where: {
+          organizationSlug,
+          OR: [
+            { status: { notIn: IN_PROGRESS } },
+            {
+              requestedAt: {
+                lt: subMinutes(requestedAt, STALE_BUILD_MINUTES),
+              },
+            },
+          ],
+        },
+        data: request,
+      })
+      if (count === 0) return null
+      await tx.walkPlanArea.deleteMany({
+        where: { walkPlan: { organizationSlug } },
+      })
+      return tx.walkPlan.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { organizationSlug } })
+    })
+    if (!reset) {
+      const existing = await this.model.findUnique({
+        where: { organizationSlug },
+        select: { id: true },
+      })
+      if (existing) {
+        throw new ConflictException('A walk plan is already being built')
+      }
+    }
+    const plan =
+      reset ??
+      (await this.model.create({ data: { organizationSlug, ...request } }))
+
+    let enqueueFailed = false
+    try {
+      await this.queueProducer.sendMessage(
+        { type: QueueType.WALK_PLAN_BUILD, data: { walkPlanId: plan.id } },
+        `${MessageGroup.walkPlanBuild}-${organizationSlug}`,
+        {
+          throwOnError: true,
+          deduplicationId: `${QueueType.WALK_PLAN_BUILD}-${plan.id}-${getTime(requestedAt)}`,
+        },
+      )
+    } catch (err) {
+      this.logger.error(
+        { err, walkPlanId: plan.id },
+        'walk plan enqueue failed',
+      )
+      enqueueFailed = true
+    }
+    if (!enqueueFailed) return toResponse(plan, [])
+
+    await this.model.updateMany({
+      where: { id: plan.id, requestedAt },
+      data: { status: WalkPlanStatus.failed },
+    })
+    return toResponse({ ...plan, status: WalkPlanStatus.failed }, [])
+  }
+
+  async handleQueuedBuild(
+    walkPlanId: number,
+    receiveCount: number,
+  ): Promise<boolean> {
+    const plan = await this.model.findFirst({
+      where: { id: walkPlanId, status: { in: IN_PROGRESS } },
+      include: { organization: true },
+    })
+    if (!plan) {
+      this.logger.info(
+        { walkPlanId },
+        'walkPlanBuild: plan is not queued or building; acking',
+      )
+      return true
+    }
+    const thisRequest = { id: walkPlanId, requestedAt: plan.requestedAt }
+
+    await this.model.updateMany({
+      where: { ...thisRequest, status: WalkPlanStatus.queued },
+      data: { status: WalkPlanStatus.building },
+    })
+
+    try {
+      const { districtId, dataset } =
+        await this.contacts.resolveEligibleDistrict(plan.organization)
+      const read = await this.voterDoorKnocking.walkPlanCells(
+        districtId,
+        dataset,
+        WALK_PLAN_MAX_CELLS,
+      )
+      const areas = await planWalkAreas(read.cells, plan.doorsPerArea)
+
+      // Stored only while the plan still answers this request, so a slow
+      // build can never overwrite a newer one. The areas are replaced whole in
+      // the same transaction that marks the plan ready: a delivery that dies
+      // before it commits leaves the plan building for the redelivery, and one
+      // after finds it ready and acks.
+      await this.client.$transaction(async (tx) => {
+        const { count } = await tx.walkPlan.updateMany({
+          where: { ...thisRequest, status: { in: IN_PROGRESS } },
+          data: {
+            status: WalkPlanStatus.ready,
+            builtAt: new Date(),
+            truncated: read.truncated,
+          },
+        })
+        if (count === 0) return
+        await tx.walkPlanArea.deleteMany({ where: { walkPlanId } })
+        for (let start = 0; start < areas.length; start += AREAS_PER_INSERT) {
+          await tx.walkPlanArea.createMany({
+            data: areas
+              .slice(start, start + AREAS_PER_INSERT)
+              .map((area, offset) => ({
+                walkPlanId,
+                ordinal: start + offset,
+                ...area,
+              })),
+          })
+        }
+      }, STORE_TRANSACTION_OPTIONS)
+    } catch (err) {
+      const lastAttempt = receiveCount >= WALK_PLAN_BUILD_MAX_RECEIVES
+      this.logger.error(
+        { err, walkPlanId, receiveCount, lastAttempt },
+        'walkPlanBuild: build failed',
+      )
+      if (!lastAttempt) return false
+      await this.model.updateMany({
+        where: { ...thisRequest, status: { in: IN_PROGRESS } },
+        data: { status: WalkPlanStatus.failed },
+      })
+    }
+    return true
+  }
+}

+import type { DbxWalkPlanCellRow } from '@/peopleDb/databricks/databricksVoterSql.util'
+
+export type PlannedWalkArea = {
+  centerLat: number
+  centerLng: number
+  households: number
+  minLat: number
+  maxLat: number
+  minLng: number
+  maxLng: number
+}
+
+type OpenArea = {
+  households: number
+  latSum: number
+  lngSum: number
+  minLat: number
+  maxLat: number
+  minLng: number
+  maxLng: number
+}
+
+// Cells between yields. A slice this size takes well under a millisecond,
+// and the build shares its event loop with the API's requests.
+const CELLS_PER_SLICE = 1_000
+
+const yieldToEventLoop = (): Promise<void> =>
+  new Promise((resolve) => setImmediate(resolve))
+
+const closeArea = (area: OpenArea): PlannedWalkArea => ({
+  centerLat: area.latSum / area.households,
+  centerLng: area.lngSum / area.households,
+  households: area.households,
+  minLat: area.minLat,
+  maxLat: area.maxLat,
+  minLng: area.minLng,
+  maxLng: area.maxLng,
+})
+
+// One pass over cells already in walking order (buildWalkPlanCellsSql):
+// each area takes the next cells until it holds at least `doorsPerArea`
+// households. A cell is never split, so a dense block can make an area
+// bigger than that, and the last area holds whatever is left. The center is
+// the households' mean position.
+export const planWalkAreas = async (
+  cells: DbxWalkPlanCellRow[],
+  doorsPerArea: number,
+): Promise<PlannedWalkArea[]> => {
+  const areas: PlannedWalkArea[] = []
+  let open: OpenArea | null = null
+  for (const [index, cell] of cells.entries()) {
+    if (index > 0 && index % CELLS_PER_SLICE === 0) await yieldToEventLoop()
+    open ??= {
+      households: 0,
+      latSum: 0,
+      lngSum: 0,
+      minLat: Infinity,
+      maxLat: -Infinity,
+      minLng: Infinity,
+      maxLng: -Infinity,
+    }
+    open.households += cell.households
+    open.latSum += cell.lat * cell.households
+    open.lngSum += cell.lng * cell.households
+    open.minLat = Math.min(open.minLat, cell.lat)
+    open.maxLat = Math.max(open.maxLat, cell.lat)
+    open.minLng = Math.min(open.minLng, cell.lng)
+    open.maxLng = Math.max(open.maxLng, cell.lng)
+    if (open.households >= doorsPerArea) {
+      areas.push(closeArea(open))
+      open = null
+    }
+  }
+  if (open) areas.push(closeArea(open))
+  return areas
+}
